title: ringswim c2 (SIBM) replicates on seed 3: ringed bean-shaped cells that move up to 5 BL; ring 1.52 (labkit) vs 1.13 at chi=0; slow, label-driven motion
summary: Fresh seed 3 of world_claim.py to t=20000: walled cells condense from noise by t=800 and persist as a bounded population of 9-17 round and bean-shaped cells with a bright L rim and a depletion wake (rerun/sheet.png). labkit radial L rim/core 1.52 with 43/62 cells membrane-like; my per-cell measure (ringmeasure.py: L within 2 px of the wall over the deep core) 1.98 (1.80-2.28), against 1.13 for world_chi0.py on the same seed (0/131 membrane-like). c07's celltrack.py: 16 track segments >= 3 BL and 1 >= 5 BL (max 5.1 BL, 0.015-0.03 px/t); world_mu0.py on the same seed: 0 >= 3 BL (max 1.8). The moving crescents carry the ring (rerun/tracks.png #464, #429).

observations.S: rerun/sheet.png t=0: smoothed noise over the whole domain; cells by t=800
observations.I: rerun/tracks.png: #7 followed from t=0 to 3000, #413 and #429 for ~2500-3000 t each as discrete walled cells
observations.B: rerun/radial.png and FACTS.md: L rim/core 1.52, 43/62 membrane-like; ring/claim_s3.json per-cell 1.98 vs ring/chi0_s3.json 1.13
observations.M: data/celltrack_claim_s3.json: 16 segments >= 3 BL, top 5.1 BL; data/celltrack_mu0_s3.json: 0 >= 3 BL

verdicts.limitation: Motion is slow (0.015-0.03 px/t) and short (16 segments >= 3 BL but only 1 >= 5 BL on this seed), and the drive is a per-body label average of the substrate gradient, i.e. a nonlocal rigid-body drift computed by the tracker labels, not a local force. No Laplacian-only twin was run for this world; in the parent phase_membrane the ring needs the chi drift (20261025T0731-c01-phase-membrane-bd-twin), which suggests B would be diffusion-testable here too. No dt or resolution check by me.
